entries.title: Monitor and manage simulation queues
entries.summary: Simulation runs now support a configurable parallel-job limit, with clear queue visibility across desktop, hosted Docker, and the dashboard.
items: Set the number of parallel simulations from Settings > Simulation Performance; Docker-hosted changes are restricted to administrators.
Monitor running and queued simulations from the global activity card, including from a simulation's own result page.
Queued simulations now clearly explain that SimC has not started, show the current queue position, and link directly to queue management instead of displaying misleading zero-progress details.
Cancel queued or running simulations directly from the activity card.
See the current queued-job count on the dashboard, which refreshes automatically while simulations are in flight.

entries.title: Connect Wishlist and Upgrade Planner
entries.summary: Wishlist targets and owned-item upgrades now follow one clear gear roadmap without duplicating entries.
items: Use Drop Finder to save gear you still need to Wishlist, then review or simulate those targets from the Wishlist page.
Open Upgrade Planner to select items already present in your SimC export and add their upgrade paths to Gear Roadmap.
See the matching character's Wishlist count and move between Drop Finder, Wishlist, and Upgrade Planner from one Upgrades navigation group.
Reorder roadmap entries, mark upgrades complete, and track planned costs against available currencies.

entries.title: Search and save Trinket result combinations
entries.summary: Upgrade Trinket results are now easier to scan and turn into Wishlist plans.
items: Search by a specific trinket name or combination to narrow the result matrix.
Save a trinket pair directly to the matching character's Wishlist; eligible upgrade trinkets are added together.
The old-season and Turbulent trinket filter appears in results only when those candidates were included when the simulation was launched.

entries.title: Share and open simulation results anywhere
entries.summary: Completed simulation results can now travel as portable `.wldps` files and open in another WhyLowDps app with the same result view.
items: Use Share result file on a completed result page, then import the file from the header or by dragging it into the web or desktop app.
On Windows, double-clicking a `.wldps` file launches WhyLowDps when it is closed or focuses the existing app when it is already running.
Shared results include the display data needed for review without requiring the original simulation job or account.

entries.title: Understand result variation at a glance
entries.summary: Result pages now place a clearer analysis section at the bottom, helping you interpret DPS variation and compare upgrades without overreacting to simulation noise.
items: View an estimated DPS distribution with P5, P25, P50, P75, and P95 percentile markers.
See a 95% confidence interval for the reported DPS mean when iteration data is available.
Compare Top Gear deltas against an uncertainty threshold labeled Meaningful, Within noise, or Needs more data.
Read stat plots against a visible baseline and compare stat weights using ranked relative bars.
The Result Insights section starts collapsed so the primary result remains the first thing you see.

entries.title: Enrich character detail pages
entries.summary: Character detail pages now bring profile, progression, profession, and external character information together in the Profile tab.
items: See active specialization, faction, guild, achievement points, item levels, Mythic+ score, highest key, top dungeon, weekly vault progress, and current-season raid progress when Blizzard provides the data.
Review primary and secondary professions with their available skill-point progress in a card styled with the character attributes.
Open consistent Armory, Warcraft Logs, and Raider.IO links for characters with spaces, apostrophes, and realm slugs.
Character data refreshes in the background after 15 minutes while the page is visible, keeps the last successful snapshot during failures, and recovers when the page becomes visible again.
Mythic+ summaries use current-season best runs when the profile index does not include period best-run entries.

entries.title: Show current raid progression
entries.summary: The character Raiding tab now displays current-season raid progress when the active raid pool identifies bosses instead of raid instances.
items: Active raid filters now match both raid instance IDs and boss encounter IDs returned by the game data context.

entries.title: Keep stable release notes synchronized
entries.summary: Stable releases promoted from a developer build now move the release notes into the versioned archive and update the app and GitHub Pages data together.
items: The promotion commit updates `master` so the published changelog cannot remain on `Unreleased` after a successful release.

entries.title: Override simulation performance per launch
entries.summary: Simulation launch controls now include a performance menu for one-time CPU thread overrides, while the main launch button continues to use the saved default.
items: Choose Balanced, Performance, or Maximum for an individual simulation without changing Settings.

entries.title: Configure simulation timeouts
entries.summary: Simulation settings now let you control how long a simulation may run and how long it may go without producing output, with a two-hour total timeout by default.
items: Adjust the total and no-output timeouts from Settings > Simulation; values are saved with your account.

entries.title: Organize settings by purpose
entries.summary: Settings are now grouped into focused tabs so simulation controls, default options, and application behavior are easier to find.
items: Default Options has its own tab, while Clipboard Import, Close Behavior, and Share over LAN are grouped under Application.
Removed the redundant Quick repairs panel in favor of the tab navigation.

entries.title: Paginate large Top Gear result lists
entries.summary: Top Gear rankings now use fixed-size pages instead of mounting every combination in one list, keeping large result sets more responsive and reducing WebView memory use.
items: Use Previous and Next to browse results; only the current page is rendered.

entries.title: Select only eligible Top Gear items
entries.summary: Top Gear now offers an Eligible quick selection that keeps equipped items and selects only alternatives valid for the active character, specialization, and item-level rules.
items: Use Eligible in the Top Gear quick actions to leave off-spec and low-level alternatives unselected.

entries.title: Keep WoW tools and custom links one click away
entries.summary: The dashboard Quick Links widget now includes popular WoW tools such as Wowhead, Raidbots, WoWAnalyzer, Warcraft Logs, and Raider.IO, with clear icons and new-tab links.
items: Add custom http:// or https:// URLs from the Quick Links editor.
Choose an icon for each custom link from the built-in icon picker; links are saved locally with the rest of the dashboard preferences.

entries.title: Persist recent SimC profile history
entries.summary: Recent SimC exports in the History list now persist locally, so they remain available after reloading the app or navigating between SimC pages.
items: History remains limited to the 20 most recent exports and can still be cleared from the profile dropdown.

entries.title: Filter legacy trinkets from Upgrade simulations
entries.summary: Upgrade Trinkets now defaults to current-season raid and dungeon sources, with an opt-in setting for old-season and Turbulent trinkets when those items are still relevant.
items: Current-season filtering is applied before simulation combinations are generated, so excluded trinkets are not simulated.
The setting can be enabled from the setup form or from the results view.

entries.title: See the exact combination count before launching
entries.summary: Top Gear and Upgrade Compare now finish calculating the full combination count before a simulation can start, and explain clearly when the total is above the configured launch limit.
items: The count continues past the configured limit so the exact total is shown.
Simulation launch stays disabled while the count is computing or above the limit.
Over-limit counts show the configured maximum and why the simulation cannot start.

entries.title: Keep simulation progress visible across pages
entries.summary: Active simulations now remain easy to monitor after navigating to another page, with a compact progress card and a completion notification when the result is ready.
items: The activity card appears on other pages and can be minimized to a small bottom-right indicator.
The duplicate activity card is hidden while viewing that simulation's own progress or result page.

entries.title: Keep long simulations and stage timing accurate
entries.summary: Simulation stage timers now use the job's persisted runtime timing, so leaving and reopening a simulation no longer resets the current stage clock. Longer simulations also have more time to finish before the total timeout is reached.
items: Stage timing remains accurate through navigation, reloads, and pause/resume.
The SimC total timeout is now two hours while the no-output timeout remains 10 minutes.

entries.title: Rework the release pipeline
entries.summary: The release pipeline now separates automated developer builds from stable release promotion for a cleaner, more reliable release cycle.
items: Pushes to `dev` publish the tested moving developer release.
Stable releases can promote the tested developer build from the Release workflow.

entries.title: Keep Full Mode after desktop updates
entries.summary: The desktop app now keeps your Light or Full Mode choice after an update, so returning players are not sent through the tour again.

entries.title: Select consumables without opening a web page
entries.summary: Consumable choices now select directly when you click their labels, while the Wowhead link is a separate, clearly marked action.

entries.title: Show the item's actual bonus stat
entries.summary: Item badges now prioritize the equipped item's bonus IDs, so bonuses such as Leech no longer appear as a stale or incorrect stat.

entries.title: Rerun simulations with their original setup
entries.summary: Rerunning a saved simulation now reuses its exact SimC input, options, item data, and specialized simulation metadata, so reruns no longer start with an empty item selection.
items: The new simulation opens on its running page immediately, keeping progress visible instead of running only in the background.

entries.title: Select restored SimC profiles automatically
entries.summary: SimC exports restored or supplied outside the profile selector now automatically select the matching saved or recent profile instead of leaving the selector blank.

entries.title: Use the selected target item level for trinket candidates
entries.summary: Trinket heatmaps now apply the selected target item level to fallback drops, preventing base-level variants from being simulated alongside the selected Myth upgrade level.
items: Myth 6/6 selections no longer add raw 108 item-level variants to a 334 target simulation.

entries.title: Show accurate Top Gear combination counts
entries.summary: Selecting all available gear items now keeps the selected item identities aligned with the resolved gear data, so the combination count no longer remains at zero during the selection update.

entries.title: Keep loot icons and selected tooltip details in sync
entries.summary: Drop Finder item cards now keep their icons visible through reliable fallback sources, while Wowhead tooltips use the selected difficulty and upgrade level so item levels and stats match the card.
items: Show a fallback icon when a primary game icon source is unavailable.
Refresh tooltip data when the selected difficulty or upgrade level changes.

releases.title: A clearer, more reliable simulation workspace

entries.title: Explore the app with guided tours
entries.summary: Page-specific tours now walk you through the dashboard, simulation, upgrade, analysis, and loot workflows when you need a quick orientation.
items: Start the current page tour from the help button in the header.
Tours can follow interactive choices and continue when the next part of a workflow opens.
Replay a completed tour whenever you want a refresher.

entries.title: Make System Health an optional dashboard widget
entries.summary: System Health no longer takes up a fixed block above the dashboard. Add it only when you want a live readiness summary alongside the other dashboard widgets.
items: Open Customize, choose Add Widget, and select System Health when you want the compact readiness summary on the board.
Drag, resize, or remove the widget like the other dashboard sections; your choice is saved locally.
Open Settings > Health for detailed diagnostics and repair actions when something needs attention.

entries.title: Choose and monitor the managed SimC runtime
entries.summary: Hosted and desktop runtime controls now expose weekly and nightly channels, available versions, update status, and safer runtime validation.
items: Select a SimC channel or a specific available runtime version from Settings > Updates.
See the active channel and version in the admin sidebar when hosted runtime controls are available.
Runtime updates validate the downloaded binary and retry incomplete manifest or release metadata before use.

entries.title: Browse the permanent changelog history
entries.summary: The full versioned release archive now lives on the generated GitHub Pages changelog, while the in-app popup stays focused on the latest update.
items: Open the archive from View changelog history in the What's New popup.
Stable releases remain linked to their original GitHub release tags.

entries.title: Keep readiness and runtime updates reliable
entries.summary: Readiness checks, staged data refreshes, managed runtime updates, and release metadata now preserve useful status and the last-known-good state when an update is incomplete.
items: See the current SimC channel and version in the admin sidebar when runtime controls are available.
Retry incomplete manifest or release metadata before activating a managed runtime update.
Validate runtime binaries before they are used for simulations.

entries.title: Use separate accounts by default
entries.summary: Battle.net users now have separate simulations, routes, profiles, history, and browser state in desktop and hosted mode. Desktop Light mode remains a persistent device-local guest account.

entries.title: Manage hosted users and Blizzard credentials
entries.summary: Hosted deployments can manage access and rotate their Blizzard application credentials without restarting the deployment.
items: Configure a BattleTag allowlist and administrator/member roles.
Disable access or revoke active sessions when needed.
Add, rotate, select, or remove hosted Blizzard application credentials at runtime.

entries.title: Install WhyLowDPS as a hosted PWA
entries.summary: The hosted web app now includes an installable manifest, service worker, offline shell, update prompt, and browser or iOS installation guidance.

entries.title: Run a private Docker-hosted instance
entries.summary: WhyLowDPS now has a prebuilt amd64 Docker deployment for private, single-instance hosting with a persistent data volume, release image pinning, health checks, and backup scripts.

entries.title: Share the desktop app over your trusted LAN
entries.summary: Desktop Settings can share WhyLowDPS with phones on the same trusted private network through one-time QR/link pairing and persistent paired-device management.

entries.title: Use WhyLowDPS comfortably on mobile
entries.summary: Navigation, action bars, dense results, settings, and dialogs now adapt to smaller touch screens, including phone safe-area support and full-height mobile flows where useful.

entries.title: Make account, dungeon, and release workflows clearer
entries.summary: Account switching, account actions, Light-mode raid browsing, dungeon fallbacks, Docker hosting, release assets, and the public hosting guides now preserve useful state and expose the important next action more clearly.

entries.title: Keep running simulations and hosted data reliable
entries.summary: Progress, profilesets, and statistics use the available page width more effectively. Hosted game-data and SimulationCraft refreshes validate staged data and retain the last-known-good state during degraded season rollovers.

entries.title: Keep simulation and account flows on the right route
entries.summary: Dungeon and Mythic+ route inputs are no longer parsed as character imports when they also contain name-like lines. Related-scenario refresh loops, account switching, and hosted Docker persistence are more reliable.

entries.title: Recent character search history
entries.summary: Find recently used characters from the header with filtering and one-click navigation.

entries.title: Pause, resume, and rerun simulations
entries.summary: Control active simulations from the result screen and rerun saved inputs in one click.

entries.title: Shared notification center
entries.summary: Review simulation results and app updates from persistent local notification history.

entries.title: Clearer running simulation status
entries.summary: Progress, profilesets, and statistics now use the available page width more effectively.

entries.title: More reliable desktop notifications
entries.summary: Completed simulation notifications are deduplicated and keep their in-app result action. App updates are recorded in notification history while the existing updater remains the live install flow.

entries.title: Setup checklist and command palette
entries.summary: Get a guided setup status and direct access to common workflows and repair areas.

entries.title: Shared active-character context
entries.summary: Keep the active character consistent between the dashboard and simulation workspace.

entries.title: Backup and restore safeguards
entries.summary: Export and restore versioned local simulation data while excluding credentials, tokens, caches, and runtime binaries.

entries.title: More reliable desktop file handoff
entries.summary: Desktop launches now accept SimC and text files through associations, drag-and-drop, and second-instance handoff.

entries.title: Clearer setup recovery
entries.summary: Setup status, repair areas, URL-addressable Settings sections, feedback semantics, and keyboard focus states are easier to find and understand.

entries.title: Season-aware Loot Browser
entries.summary: Group loot by expansion, season, and the active dungeon rotation.

entries.title: Resizable Loot Browser instance panel
entries.summary: Resize the instance panel with mouse or keyboard controls.

entries.title: More stable historical dungeon views
entries.summary: Active dungeons stay in the active group, source-expansion links remain available, current-season item-level controls are preserved, and incomplete metadata uses trusted fallbacks.

entries.title: Repository governance documentation
entries.summary: Added the project license, contribution guide, security policy, code of conduct, and roadmap.

entries.title: Clearer raid-buff source badges
entries.summary: Hover explanations now clarify Override, Manual, and Default sources.

entries.title: A less disruptive What's New popup
entries.summary: The in-app changelog no longer blocks Windows title-bar controls or window dragging.

entries.title: Structured release notes and downloads
entries.summary: Release artifacts include a recommended download, SHA256 checksums, and explicit Windows, SmartScreen, and Battle.net credential notes.

entries.title: Discord invite and quick links
entries.summary: A first-launch Discord invite and sidebar links make community access easier.
